name: SQL/PSM
title: SQL/PSM (MySQL 9.7)

type.text: **NULL is a member of every domain**: a routine parameter, local, or OUT value carries NULL without a declaration, three-valued logic decides every comparison, and no signature states whether NULL is legal
**No sum types**: an alternative is modeled by nullable OUT parameters, a status column, or separate routines, and the caller learns the encoding by reading the body
**No generic parameter**: routines are typed per definition, and a routine over "any table" must take dynamic SQL or return one fixed shape

**Statements state no effect**: a stored function that writes a table, calls a trigger, or reads the clock looks like any other in the catalog — only the DETERMINISTIC/NOT DETERMINISTIC declaration, which the docs state is trusted for replication rather than verified, says anything
**C code rides the boundary**: the server loads native plugins and UDFs through its plugin interface, and the declaration the two sides agree on is checked by neither compiler

construction.text: **The routine is one block**: BEGIN ... END gathers DECLARE, flow, and SQL into one deployable unit the catalog stores and parses
**Tables mutate in place**: the routine body is ordinary DML, and every UPDATE is an in-place mutation with no immutability construct anywhere in the language

memory.text: **Allocation is the server's**: buffers, sort areas, and cursors live in mysqld, and the routine text allocates nothing

error.text: **The handler decides, or the statement dies**: DECLARE ... HANDLER FOR SQLEXCEPTION routes a failure, and without a handler the routine aborts with an error to the caller — no value ever carries the failure
**No composable result type**: failures travel by exception or error code, results by OUT parameters and SELECT result sets, and neither can thread through an expression

concurrency.text: **One session, one shared state**: user variables, temporary tables, and session settings are visible across every routine the session calls, so two callers of the same routine share what it reads

platform.text: **The routine runs only in MySQL-family servers**: CALL speaks the server's protocol, the body compiles in the server's parser, and nothing in the language runs without mysqld
**A poor fit outside set work**: the language has no data abstraction beyond tables, no libraries, and no error values, so application logic pays for every abstraction it builds

performance.text: **The plan is inspectable**: EXPLAIN answers for the statements inside a routine through the ordinary session tools, and the optimizer answers per statement

ecosystem.text: **The installed base is one of the largest**: drivers, ORMs, admin tooling, and managed offerings surround the server, and the community forums and docs answer the common questions

evolution.text: **The LTS calendar governs the surface**: 9.7 is the newest long-term-support line, the release model states that features change only in the first release of an LTS line, and maintenance arrives quarterly

domain.text: **The routine exists to serve the database**: the catalog, the privilege model, and the trigger/event system define what a stored program is, and moving the logic moves the engine

learning.text: **SQL-92 roots with procedural grafts**: the docs interleave ISO statements with MySQL-specific variables, handlers, and delimiters, and the traps (implicit commits, cursor scoping) get their own chapters

syntax.text: **The tool changes the text**: DELIMITER is a client-side convention the server never sees, one of several places where the program's meaning depends on which tool reads it
**Case rules differ per layer**: table and column case follows the file system on some platforms while routine names follow the server, and the docs devote a page to identifier case sensitivity

testing.text: **No standard test harness for user routines**: mysqltest serves the server's own suite, and the documented testing story for stored programs is application-side tests against a live server

security.text: **Dynamic SQL is string-built**: PREPARE and EXECUTE run SQL text held in a variable, so concatenated user input reaches the parser, and the documented mitigation is SQL-level privileges plus bound parameters
**SQL SECURITY DEFINER runs as its owner**: a definer routine executes with the owner's privileges, so the catalog records a trust decision the body never states

reproducibility.text: **A routine is stored source**: the same body on the same server version and data reproduces the same result, and nothing is compiled ahead of the call
**No toolchain pin exists**: the repository names no server version — the executing release is a deployment fact a third-party manager must supply

supplychain.text: **No signed provenance for published routines or plugins**: routines move as SQL dumps the server executes, and plugins install from distribution channels without signature checks

**No advisory feed names stored-program issues**: fixes land in quarterly LTS release notes, and no published advisory database tracks the language surface the way Apache and CNCF projects publish theirs

observability.text: **No tracing standard is part of the language**: the performance_schema and the general log are server features, and the routine text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: SIGNAL text and the server log are all a routine can emit, and no logging construct exists in the language

feedback.text: **No routine debugger ships with the server**: diagnosis goes through SELECT scaffolding, handler instrumentation, and the error message

interop.text: **No portable target**: the body compiles in one server family's parser, and SQL/PSM conformance is a manual claim no suite checks

governance.text: **Governance is Oracle**: the release model, the LTS calendar, and the language's direction are one company's, and no independent body can change them
**No public specification exists**: the reference manual documents the implemented behavior of one server line, and no independent implementation follows from a published standard document
**Correctness is what mysqld does**: no conformance suite exists for the stored-program language, and a second implementation would be a compatibility gamble

tradeoffs: **Logic next to the data**: routines remove the network round trip per statement and run inside the server's transactions, and the price is application logic whose deploy, debug, and version story is the database's

**Handlers are optional by design**: BEGIN ... END with DECLARE ... HANDLER gives structured recovery, and the price is that a routine without one fails at the first unhandled error, discovered by the caller
**Session state is the shared resource**: user variables and temporary tables make cross-routine state cheap, and the price is that every caller of a routine shares whatever the session already holds
**The definer is a privilege decision**: SQL SECURITY DEFINER lets one routine guard a table behind its owner's rights, and the price is a trust edge the signature carries silently
verdict: MySQL's stored-program language is SQL/PSM-shaped procedural SQL: BEGIN ... END blocks over DECLARE, cursors, handlers, SIGNAL and dynamic PREPARE, deployed as procedures, functions, triggers, and events inside the server catalog. Its costs are the server family's own: NULL in every domain with no null-safety, failures that travel only by exception or error code, session-wide user variables and temporary tables as the default shared state, and single-vendor governance with no specification and no conformance suite. Main strengths: one deployable block per program, structured handler-based recovery, EXPLAIN through the ordinary session tools, GPL-public source, and a release model (9.7 LTS, quarterly maintenance) the docs state plainly. Main weaknesses: no debugger or user-routine test harness, no structured logging or tracing in the language, string-built dynamic SQL as the standing injection surface, and logic whose reproducibility depends on a server version no repository file names.

energy.text: Energy is mysqld's: buffer pool, sort areas, and the event scheduler pay, and the reader's levers are index and statement design the routine text exposes but does not control.

ai-readiness.text: Generated stored programs are common in migrations and admin tooling, and the traps are exactly the procedural layer: handler scope, implicit commits, definer rights, and cursor state that no generated snippet names.

safety.text: No certified path; InnoDB's ACID guarantees and the privilege model are the server's, stated in its own documentation.

use:data.observation: the routine body is ordinary DML

use:query.observation: results by OUT parameters and SELECT result sets

delivery.target: stored program source (procedures, functions, triggers, events)
delivery.note: the database stores the source text and parses it at creation and use; no compiled unit crosses a boundary
